headline: Kai, the shrug is over — futures are red, oil is pushing $88, and markets now lean toward a September hike.
subline: Trump threatened to hit Iran 'hard' after the weekend exchange, JOLTS and ISM manufacturing land this morning, and hike odds sit near 68%.
asof: Pre-market · index futures as of 5:00 AM ET, yields & bitcoin ~6:40 · every figure links to its source below

items.title: September hike odds climb toward 68%
items.sentence: Trading Economics puts market-implied odds of a September hike near 68% after Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole inflation warning, with the 10-year up about three basis points at 4.79% as dearer oil feeds the case.

items.title: Oil extends gains; futures open September lower
items.sentence: Yahoo Finance quotes WTI up 2.32% at $87.75 on fears of another U.S.–Iran round, with S&P 500 futures off 0.57%, Nasdaq 100 futures down 1.02%, and gold easing 1.30% to $4,423.40.

items.title: JOLTS, ISM manufacturing and four earnings reports today
items.sentence: Yahoo Finance's calendar has JOLTS job openings, ISM manufacturing and construction spending this morning, with Dell, Palo Alto Networks, Medtronic and MongoDB reporting after the bell.

items.title: A red Monday still sealed a winning August
items.sentence: The S&P 500 slipped 0.33% to 7,686.14 and the Dow lost 374 points Monday, but the Dow still booked a fifth straight monthly gain and the Nasdaq added about 3.9% in August, per STL.News.

items.title: Bitcoin enters September near $78,300
items.sentence: CoinGecko has bitcoin at $78,301 this morning, up 0.2% over 24 hours and about 38% below last October's $126,080 peak. It gets there off an August that Bitcoin.com News counts among its best months of 2026 — a rebound that repaired most of this year's drawdown.

items.title: Trump threatens to hit Iran 'hard' as strikes resume
items.sentence: U.S. forces struck Iranian rocket launchers near the Strait of Hormuz in the first exchange between the two in a month, and Trump warned he would respond 'hard,' per NBC News.

items.title: Tankers struck in the Strait of Hormuz
items.sentence: CBS News reports commercial tankers were hit in the strait as Trump weighs further strikes in what he calls a 'relatively little war.'

items.title: U.S. takes majority stake in Venezuelan oil
items.sentence: The administration announced a deal giving the U.S. a majority stake in Venezuela's oil reserves, though energy experts doubt it will do much for pump prices, per NPR.

items.title: House returns with a stopgap bill on deck
items.sentence: Congress is back from recess with a temporary spending measure atop the agenda, per NPR.

items.title: Jury convicts Duane Davis of Tupac Shakur's murder
items.sentence: A jury found Davis guilty of orchestrating the 1996 killing of the rap icon, resolving a case three decades old, per NPR.

items.title: Pentagon opens GenAI.mil, with Claude conspicuously absent
items.sentence: ChatGPT Mil and Grok for Government joined Gemini on the Pentagon's secure portal for three million personnel — 1.7 million already onboarded — while Anthropic remains excluded under its 'supply-chain risk' label, per TechCrunch.

items.title: Judge voids the Pentagon's Anthropic blacklist
items.sentence: A federal judge ruled that supply-chain-risk designation unlawful, per CNN — the company's first court win in the dispute.

items.title: Nvidia pauses its $36 billion AI-cloud financing
items.sentence: Nvidia suspended its AI Compute Partnership revenue-sharing model — about $36 billion in disclosed commitments — amid antitrust scrutiny and partner pushback, per Techstrong.ai.

items.title: DeepSeek open-sources its first native vision model
items.sentence: DeepSeek published open weights for V4-Flash-Vision-Exp, the experimental multimodal model it claims brings agent performance close to Anthropic's Opus 4.8, per Open Source For You and The Next Web.

items.title: Runway's Solaris draws working interfaces frame by frame
items.sentence: Runway unveiled Solaris, an 'interface world model' that generates interactive apps in real time with no code, per the company's research note.
